name: nonApi_getUserInviteCode
description: Internal, no auth. Called only by the EmailInviteCode Azure Function (api/Endpoints/EmailInviteCode.cs) — never by the app or portal. Resolves the live hasher (Removed = 0) for @email, calls HC6.nonApi_ensureUserInviteCode with @rotateIfOlderThanMinutes = 10080 so the hasher holds a compliant 'URC:' + six-letter code that lives a WEEK (2026-10-04: it was 60 minutes, and asking again an hour later killed the code already sent), then returns the code with the 'URC:' prefix stripped — or a human-readable not-found sentence. Asking again within the week returns the same code.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address of the hasher requesting an invite code. Table column is NVARCHAR(250) NOT NULL.

rowsets.name: InviteCodeResult
rowsets.description: Always returns exactly 1 row. On success: the 6-letter invite code. On email-not-found: a human-readable message string. Callers must distinguish success from failure by examining whether the value looks like a 6-letter code or a sentence.

columns.name: inviteCode
columns.description: The six-letter code ('URC:' stripped), or 'The email address provided was not found in our database. Please try another email address.' when no live hasher has that address. NVARCHAR(50) on success; the COALESCE widens to fit the sentence.

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.nonApi_ensureUserInviteCode @userId, @rotateIfOlderThanMinutes = 10080 — may UPDATE HC.Hasher.ResetCode / ResetCodeLastUpdated (a non-compliant code, or a compliant one older than a week, is replaced), which fires the Hasher triggers (updatedAt; trgGenerateQrCode re-validates ResetCode).

codeSmells.issue: SP body not wrapped in TRY/CATCH
codeSmells.detail: Lines 34-59 have no TRY/CATCH. The helper logs its own errors and re-throws, but an error in the lookups here (lines 35, 54) reaches EmailInviteCode as a raw exception with no HC.ErrorLog row from this SP (CLAUDE.md 'TRY/CATCH is mandatory on EVERY SP').
@email (line 2) has no SQL default. The one C# caller always supplies it.

codeSmells.issue: Success vs. error indistinguishable from rowset shape alone
codeSmells.detail: Both paths return one inviteCode column (lines 56-59); EmailInviteCode must inspect the value to tell a code from the not-found sentence.

codeSmells.issue: Email lookup is not deterministic when two live accounts share an address
codeSmells.detail: Line 35 assigns from SELECT … WHERE email = @email AND Removed = 0 with no ORDER BY; IX on Email is not unique-filtered on Removed, so a duplicate live address picks an arbitrary account.

codeSmells.issue: ResetCode is also policed by trgGenerateQrCode
codeSmells.detail: The HC.Hasher trigger (db/schema/tables/HC.Hasher.Table.sql lines 194-244) rewrites ResetCode when it collides or lacks 'URC:'. The helper always writes a unique 'URC:' value, so they agree today; two places now define a valid code.

breakingChanges: HC5 contained a hardcoded email override (james@jamesawhite.com → 'NCCARY'). HC6 removes this testing backdoor.
HC5 inlined HC.NUMBER_TO_STR_BASE scalar function. HC6 replaces it with an inline WHILE loop using SUBSTRING(alphabet, ...) for direct uppercase-letter generation.

1.1.0 (2026-09-07 / 2026-10-04): generation moved to HC6.nonApi_ensureUserInviteCode (a non-compliant code such as '######' is replaced, not handed out); the reuse window went from 60 minutes to one week (10080). Rowset unchanged.
